title: Boss: search and sort
summary: Binary search on answers and rotated arrays, counting inversions with merge sort, and a one-pass partition.

steps.title: Square root by bisection
prompt: Binary search works on any yes/no question that flips once. "Is `m × m <= n`?" is yes for small `m` and no for big `m`.
Write `int SqrtFloor(int n)` for `n >= 0`: the largest `m` with `m * m <= n`. No `Math.Sqrt` or `Math.Pow`.
Careful: `m * m` overflows `int` for big `m`; compute it as a `long`.
solution: if (mid * mid <= n) { best = mid; lo = mid + 1; }
template: for (var dojoI = 0; dojoI < 300_000; dojoI++) dojoSum += SqrtFloor(dojoI * 7000);

forbid.message: Does not use Math.Sqrt or Math.Pow

hints: Search `m` between 0 and `n`. When `mid * mid <= n`, remember `mid` as the best so far and search right; otherwise search left.

steps.title: Search a rotated array
prompt: A sorted array of **distinct** numbers was rotated: `{ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 }` became `{ 5, 6, 7, 1, 2, 3, 4 }`. Write `int SearchRotated(int[] a, int target)`: its index, or `-1`, in `O(log n)`.

At every `mid`, **one half is still sorted**. If `a[lo] <= a[mid]` the left half `lo..mid` is sorted: if the target lies inside its range, search there, otherwise search the right. Otherwise the right half `mid..hi` is sorted: same idea, mirrored.
The tests run 200,000 searches, so a linear scan is too slow.
solution: if (a[lo] <= target && target < a[mid]) hi = mid - 1;
if (a[mid] < target && target <= a[hi]) lo = mid + 1;
template: for (var dojoT = 0; dojoT < 200_000; dojoT++) dojoSum += SearchRotated(dojoBig, dojoT * 5);
Dojo.Eq("200,000 searches on a million items", dojoWant, dojoSum);
hints: Decide which half is sorted by comparing `a[lo]` with `a[mid]`.
In the sorted half you can test `a[lo] <= target && target < a[mid]` (or the mirror for the right side) to know whether the target is inside it.

steps.title: Count inversions
prompt: An **inversion** is a pair `i < j` with `a[i] > a[j]`: it measures how unsorted an array is. `{ 2, 4, 1, 3, 5 }` has 3: (2,1), (4,1), (4,3).
Write `long CountInversions(int[] a)`. Checking every pair is `O(n²)`, and the tests use 200,000 numbers.
Piggyback on merge sort: while merging, whenever you take an item from the **right** half, it is smaller than every item still waiting in the left half. Add `left.Length - i` to the count.
solution: else { count += l.Length - i; result[k++] = r[j++]; }
template: Dojo.Eq("equal values are not inversions", 0L, CountInversions(new[] { 2, 2, 2 }));
hints: Write merge sort as a local function inside `CountInversions` so it can add to a `count` variable.
In the merge, the `else` branch (taking `r[j]`) is where `count += l.Length - i;` goes. Use `<=` so equal values are not counted.

steps.title: Three-way partition
prompt: An array holds only `0`, `1` and `2`. Write `void SortColors(int[] a)` that sorts it **in one pass**, in place, without counting first and without library sorts.
Keep three regions with pointers `low`, `mid` and `high`: `a[..low]` is all 0s, `a[low..mid]` all 1s, `a[high + 1..]` all 2s, and `a[mid..high]` is still unknown.
- `a[mid] == 2`: swap it with `a[high]`, then `high--` (do **not** move `mid`: the swapped-in value is unchecked).
template: Dojo.Eq("300,000 items: the first 1 is at 100,000", 100_000, Array.IndexOf(dojoBig, 1));
Dojo.Eq("300,000 items: the first 2 is at 200,000", 200_000, Array.IndexOf(dojoBig, 2));

forbid.message: Does not call a library sort

hints: Follow the three rules exactly. The 2 case swaps with `high` and leaves `mid` where it is.
